title: Microsoft Dataverse: run prompt columns on existing records in bulk (backfill)
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap record and Microsoft Learn. The environment controls, automation call, credit consumption and job limits check out, and the briefing explicitly reports the documentation's differing rollout and import-support statements.

claims.claim: The bulk-processing gate is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Allow bulk processing of existing records.
claims.quote:
Two environment settings in the [Power Platform admin center](https://admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com/) control this option. Select your environment and go to **Settings** > **Features**.

- **Allow bulk processing of existing records**: This setting is off by default.

claims.claim: The bulk-processing and imported-job review settings apply per environment.

claims.claim: The job updates the corresponding Status and Details columns as each record completes.
claims.quote: The system updates the prompt column, along with its **Status** and **Details** columns, as each record completes.

claims.claim: The existing prompt column execution model runs on record creation or an update to referenced input columns.
claims.quote: Prompt column values are populated when records are created and when the input column values are updated. When prompt columns are added to tables with records, the existing records' new prompt columns aren't populated automatically.

claims.claim: The FAQ says changing a prompt definition does not recalculate existing values until a later update to a referenced column.
claims.quote: updating the prompt definition does not recalculate existing prompt values until a subsequent update occurs on one or more columns defined in the prompt.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents bulk backfill as rolling out and potentially unavailable in the reader's region, despite the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: This capability is in process of rolling out, and might not be available in your region yet.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Capacity
claims.claim: Microsoft tells administrators to ensure sufficient environment AI credit capacity before enabling bulk processing.
claims.quote: Ensure sufficient AI credit capacity is available in the environment before enabling it.

claims.claim: The AI model processes a prompt using the specified input columns.
claims.quote: The AI model processes these prompts to generate relevant responses based on specified input columns.

claims.claim: Generated prompt column results are stored persistently in the Dataverse table.
claims.quote: The key function is that the prompt column contains generative AI results stored in the table persistently.

claims.claim: Microsoft's prompts overview says prompts use models powered by Azure Foundry.
claims.quote: Prompts use models powered by [Azure Foundry](/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure).

claims.claim: Access to the generated prompt column matters separately from access to its source columns.
claims.quote: data might be displayed in the calculated or prompt column to users that don't have permission to the secured column. Both the original column and the calculated or prompt column should be secured.

claims.claim: Prompt column execution can fail when the user lacks sufficient permissions on an input column.
claims.quote: The user doesn't have sufficient permissions on one or more input columns referenced in the prompt column definition.
